title: Distinguish valid-input requirements from descriptions of rejected values
applies_when: A candidate alleges a reversed error message because its comparison word appears opposite to the enclosing rejection guard, especially numeric limit or capacity diagnostics.
lesson: Read the complete guard and diagnostic together before preparing a native environment. A requirement describes the accepted set, not the observed rejected value: count >= N is consistent with 'needs fewer than N'. Replacing that requirement with 'needs more than N' would invert it. Check exact boundary equality as well as the direction. Retain a source-grounded stop and its reopening condition instead of manufacturing a regression that asserts the proposed wording.
avoid_when: Messages describing actual observations, such as 'received too few', follow different semantics from requirements. A documented exact-message contract or genuinely ambiguous actionable instruction can warrant a fix. This source-only counterexample rejects one diagnostic allegation; it establishes neither runtime reachability nor native/GPU/kernel correctness, performance or measured Scout conversion gains. Do not use it to reject other candidates without inspecting their guards and wording.

evidence.note: The complete _attention_unit_costs function rejects seg_clusters >= ATTN_MAX_SEGMENT_CLUSTERS and says a segment needs fewer than that limit. The module defines the limit as 1 << 16. The requirement direction is correct; no native import or GPU test is needed to refute this specific inverted-wording proposal.
